scope: Twelve proposed component tests, not twelve demonstrations of the universal hypothesis. These specifications were written after consulting published studies and are not preregistrations.

cases.title: The Square with One Answer
cases.case: Napoleonic blockade and French mechanized cotton spinning
cases.claim_tested: A trade bottleneck can make a previously uncompetitive local assembly viable.
cases.assignment: Geographic differences in exposure to the wartime blockade, 1806–1814; exposure is not randomly assigned.
cases.design: Regional changes in mechanized spinning capacity, 1803 to 1812, regressed on predetermined blockade exposure and baseline capacity.
cases.window: period 0 = 1803; period 1 = 1812. Outcome = mechanized spindles per region. Exposure = documented regional trade-protection measure, not a label inferred from adoption.
cases.counterfactual: Less exposed French regions; use the paper's exposure construction and geographic units consistently.
cases.prediction: More exposed regions increase mechanized capacity more, conditional on baseline capacity.
diagnostics: Document exposure construction and geographic clustering
Compare baseline industrial capacity and geography
Repeat with alternative pre-specified trade-cost controls; investigate direct wartime destruction
identification_limits: Geography, war damage, demand, and protection may jointly change
Only two snapshots do not establish parallel pretrends
Profitability of adoption does not measure creative search or entropy maximization
cases.data_status: Replication archive identified but returned HTTP 403 in this environment. Adapter needs a documented regional extract; it is not a reproduction of every published specification.

cases.title: The Gradient and the Barrier
cases.case: Japan's electricity mix after the 2011 Tohoku disaster and nuclear shutdowns
cases.claim_tested: Closing an established energy pathway redirects production through other pathways.
cases.assignment: Earthquake, tsunami, plant damage, and subsequent policy responses constitute a compound shock.
cases.design: Synthetic-control comparison, Japan versus a fixed donor pool; 2000–2010 preperiod, 2011–2015 postperiod; 2009–2010 held-out preperiod validation.
cases.primary_outcome: Fossil share of electricity, percentage points
cases.secondary_outcome: Nuclear share of electricity, percentage points
cases.counterfactual: A convex combination of the named countries; Germany excluded because of its contemporaneous nuclear policy shift.
cases.prediction: Nuclear share falls and fossil share increases relative to the fitted comparison.
diagnostics: Pre-fit error and held-out preperiod fit
Leave-one-donor-out sensitivity
Donor placebo gaps and fit quality
Electricity shares do not quantify useful energy or total demand
identification_limits: Earthquake damage and demand changes cannot be separated from the nuclear response
Other countries may respond to the same disaster
One treated country: placebo ranks are not randomization p-values
Substitution does not establish an entropy-production maximum
cases.data_status: Public annual data; executable comparison, causal interpretation conditional on unverified counterfactual assumptions.

cases.title: Life Makes Its Conditions
cases.case: Northern California kelp collapse after predator loss and marine heatwaves
cases.claim_tested: Disruption of ecological maintenance can produce persistent loss of a living system's conditions of continuation.
cases.assignment: 2013 sea-star wasting disease and 2014–2016 marine heatwaves; exposure and biological vulnerability vary geographically.
cases.design: Matched-site change comparison: 2008–2012 versus 2017–2019 mean canopy area, with exposure fixed by independently measured disease/thermal stress rather than subsequent kelp loss.
cases.window: period 0 = mean annual canopy hectares 2008–2012; period 1 = 2017–2019. Use fixed survey polygons and coverage. Match on pre-shock trends, species, depth, and wave exposure.
cases.counterfactual: Less exposed, pretrend-comparable sites with the same kelp species; do not automatically equate southern giant kelp with northern bull kelp.
cases.prediction: Maintenance disruption predicts persistent canopy loss after the immediate shock.
diagnostics: Plot site pretrends before constructing window means
Separate temperature from predator-loss exposure
Check survey effort, species, and missing coverage
Cluster by independent coastal exposure region
identification_limits: No verified exchangeable control group has yet been assembled
Disease and heatwave are compound exposures
Ecological regeneration is an analogue, not proof that an ecosystem is an autopoietic organism
cases.data_status: Public Dryad inventory located; downloads returned HTTP 401/403. Historical kelp data alone do not supply independent exposure or credible controls. Needs a harmonized site panel.

cases.title: The Discovery That Became Possible
cases.case: Unexpected deaths of leading scientists and collaborators' output
cases.claim_tested: Interrupting an established knowledge network changes what its surviving members can produce.
cases.assignment: Unexpected death while scientifically active; foreseeable illness and retirement require exclusion or separate treatment.
cases.design: Matched scientist-network change comparison, frozen collaborators and matches selected before death; star-specific calendar windows and matched-set fixed effects.
cases.window: period 0 = mean annual publications in event years -5 through -1; period 1 = +1 through +5. Unit = pre-death collaborator network, cluster = deceased/matched star, stratum = matched set. Death year excluded.
cases.counterfactual: Matched networks of still-active, similar scientists observed in the same calendar years.
cases.prediction: Loss of an active collaborator depresses output beyond the counterfactual trend.
diagnostics: Pre-death trends, death predictability, collaborator selection
Handle overlapping networks before aggregation
Check field-wide funding and topic shocks
identification_limits: Illness anticipation, grants, and personnel moves may confound effects
Network interference violates independent-cluster assumptions
Tests knowledge dependence, not simultaneous relativity discovery or its thermodynamic cause
cases.data_status: Published design identified; no usable public matched panel located. Requires a documented bibliometric extract.

cases.title: How Disequilibrium Builds a New Pathway
cases.claim_tested: Making an energy pathway available can change productive participation.
cases.assignment: Terrain slope changes the cost of extending the electricity grid; use it as an instrument only under an explicit exclusion restriction.
cases.design: Community-level two-stage least squares: change in female employment on electrification, instrumented by terrain slope, with baseline controls.
cases.counterfactual: Communities induced into electrification by lower construction costs, conditional on observed preconditions.
cases.prediction: Electrification increases female employment where the instrument affects access.
diagnostics: Cluster first-stage strength and reduced form
Slope may directly affect agriculture, transport, and local development
Compare baseline covariates and alternative controls before causal interpretation
identification_limits: Exclusion and monotonicity are assumptions, not consequences of first-stage strength
Local IV effect, not a population-wide law
Modern analogue; does not identify why the first steam engine appeared in England rather than China
cases.data_status: AEA archive located but HTTP 403. Needs a documented community extract; adapter is a component analysis, not the original paper's complete replication.

cases.title: Could the Laws Have a History?
cases.claim_tested: A model predicting changes in the fine-structure constant must respect isotope-based constraints.
cases.assignment: Ancient nuclear reaction conditions supply a physical record, not a treatment/control assignment for the birth of the universe.
cases.design: Compare a proposed fractional change in alpha against a published conditional 95% bound; no raw-isotope re-estimation.
cases.counterfactual: A specified varying-alpha history evaluated against the isotope record and nuclear sensitivity model.
cases.prediction: Any proposed assembly model that also predicts late-time drift must satisfy this conditional bound or explain why its assumptions fail.
diagnostics: Check nuclear-model assumptions
Check restrictions on simultaneous changes in quark-mass/QCD-scale ratios
Do not derive a drift rate without a time dependence model
identification_limits: The bound is conditional on the source's restriction relating changes in other fundamental parameters
No likelihood, new confidence interval, or raw isotope analysis is supplied
Constancy after formation neither proves nor refutes assembled origins
No credible natural experiment identifies the creation of the universe or its constants
cases.data_status: Published-summary constraint available. The chapter's origin claim remains unidentified; optional model predictions can be checked.

cases.title: The Species That Changed Its Own Conditions
cases.claim_tested: Changes in a socially maintained developmental environment can alter measured cognitive performance.
cases.assignment: Municipal adoption of nine-year compulsory schooling, phased in during 1955–1972; treatment depends on birth cohort and municipality.
cases.design: Cohort-specific difference-in-differences using never/not-yet-treated municipalities; no already-treated controls or ordinary staggered TWFE.
cases.window: unit = municipality; period = birth cohort, not examination year; adoption = first birth cohort exposed to reform (0 = never treated); outcome = cohort mean conscript IQ on one consistent scale. Include at least two pre-cohorts and five post-cohorts.
cases.counterfactual: Same birth cohorts in municipalities that have not yet adopted, compared with g-1; g-2 to g-1 placebo contrast.
cases.prediction: Exposed cohorts have improved test performance relative to the local counterfactual.
diagnostics: Pre-reform cohort differences and anticipation
Municipal adoption timing, migration, and test participation
Use consistent IQ scale and age
Report changing cohort composition
identification_limits: Municipal rollout may correlate with changing conditions
Adapter gives unadjusted cohort points, without inference; not the original IV specification
Male conscript sample limits generalization
Cannot identify ancient genetic self-domestication or its proposed violence mechanism
cases.data_status: Requires authorized administrative microdata or a vetted municipality/cohort extract; no such extract is in this repository.

cases.title: The World That Learned to Think
cases.case: Maimonides' class-size rule in Israeli schools
cases.claim_tested: A formal rule changes the material organization of teaching and can change learning outcomes.
cases.assignment: Enrollment moving from 40 to 41 is meant to split a grade into two classes; actual class size is imperfectly compliant.
cases.design: Fuzzy local-linear regression discontinuity at enrollment 40.5, triangular weights, separate slopes, school-clustered inference. Bandwidth 10 primary; 5 and 15 sensitivity.
cases.counterfactual: Schools just below versus just above the first enrollment threshold.
cases.prediction: The threshold reduces class size; additional pupils per class lower scores locally if the proposed support mechanism operates.
diagnostics: First-stage size and clustered t-squared
Disadvantage-index discontinuity and enrollment counts
Fixed bandwidth sensitivity
Author data corrections and sample restrictions are explicit
identification_limits: Enrollment manipulation and other discontinuous policies threaten identification
Integer enrollment makes continuous-density tests inappropriate without modification
Conventional Wald interval suppressed when first stage is weak or there are few schools
Local class-size effect, not genetic intelligence or thermodynamic optimization
cases.data_status: Public author Stata data and original cleaning instructions. Reanalysis at the first cutoff, not a replication of all published tables.

cases.title: The System That Produces Its Tomorrow
cases.case: New Jersey's 1992 minimum-wage increase versus Pennsylvania
cases.claim_tested: A changed material wage guarantee need not undermine employment in the sector sustaining it.
cases.assignment: New Jersey policy change; adjacent Pennsylvania has no equivalent increase at that date.
cases.design: Two-wave restaurant employment difference-in-differences from the author survey archive; report balanced-pair and confirmed-closure sensitivity.
cases.counterfactual: Pennsylvania fast-food restaurants surveyed in the same waves.
cases.prediction: If the higher wage guarantee disrupts this productive loop, employment should fall relative to the comparison; no fall rejects that narrow prediction.
diagnostics: Missing pre/post staffing and closure status by state
Balanced-pair versus confirmed-closure coding
Baseline differences and chains
No pretrend check is possible from two waves
identification_limits: Only two state-level policy assignments: restaurant-level standard errors are not policy-level uncertainty
State-specific shocks and survey error remain possible
One employment outcome cannot establish institutional closure, money's origin, or feudalism's collapse
cases.data_status: Public author archive. Descriptive DiD point estimates; no policy-level p-value or confidence interval.

cases.title: The System That Models Itself
cases.case: Daylight-saving transitions and fatal road crashes
cases.claim_tested: Disrupting a maintenance schedule can impair subsequent regulated performance.
cases.assignment: Legally scheduled spring clock changes, including the 2007 US rule change; Arizona/Hawaii do not observe DST statewide.
cases.design: Within-year difference-in-differences comparing mean daily fatal crashes in weeks -2/-1 and +1/+2 in DST and non-DST states, omitting transition day.
cases.window: Full daily state counts 2000–2015, including real zero-crash days; events use first Sunday of April through 2006, second Sunday of March from 2007. Exclude Indiana and geographically mixed DST observations; confirm AZ tribal exclusions before using the state aggregate.
cases.counterfactual: Non-DST states observed on the same calendar dates, with day-of-week-balanced windows.
cases.prediction: Fatal crashes rise immediately after sleep disruption, conditional on driving exposure and other temporal changes.
diagnostics: Pre-event placebo windows
Driving exposure, daylight, weather, holidays
2007 date change separates some seasonal mechanisms
State policy assignment has very few untreated clusters
identification_limits: Clock changes alter daylight as well as sleep; crashes do not directly measure maintenance or cognition
Arizona tribal exceptions complicate state aggregates
This adapter gives yearly point contrasts, not a replication of Smith's richer design
Does not identify self-modeling, consciousness, or the complete autopoietic loop
cases.data_status: FARS primary data source and replication archive identified; no harmonized daily extract available here. Adapter requires documented coverage and DST classification.

cases.title: Why the World Builds Artificial Intelligence
cases.claim_tested: Use of an AI service depends on externally maintained access; removing it may change productive behavior or trigger substitution.
cases.assignment: Country-level legal restriction with imperfect compliance, anticipation, and VPN substitution.
cases.design: Primary: daily coding-output synthetic control from a fixed pre-ban developer cohort. Available secondary diagnostic: official Tor estimated-user series, Italy versus France, Germany, Spain, UK, Sweden.
cases.window: Primary preperiod Jan 1–Mar 30, 2023; postperiod Mar 31–Apr 27. Country codes it/fr/de/es/gb/se. Outcome = daily contributions per fixed pre-ban active developer, with an explicitly documented fixed denominator. Tor uses common observed dates only and audits gaps.
cases.counterfactual: A fixed European donor pool; no outcome-driven selection of countries or developer cohorts.
cases.prediction: Blocking a useful service changes exposed developers' work; circumvention may rise. The latter is a separate secondary prediction.
diagnostics: Pre-fit and held-out preperiod fit
Leave-one-country-out and donor placebos
Country-series missingness
Separate heterogeneous coding effects from circumvention
One country cannot supply user-level policy assignment inference
identification_limits: Tor users are not ChatGPT users, and Tor is not all VPN activity
The Tor comparison cannot estimate coding productivity or model cognition
Other country-specific shocks and international spillovers remain
Access effects cannot establish infinite cognition, trained reasoning mechanisms, or AI inevitability
cases.data_status: Tor secondary data are public. Primary coding panel still needed; the secondary run is explicitly descriptive.

cases.title: The Machines That Build the Next Machines
cases.claim_tested: Loss and restoration of physical infrastructure changes the availability of computation.
cases.assignment: Unanticipated facility fire; tenant placement, backups, and network routing are not random.
cases.design: Primary: matched-service availability changes for preidentified Strasbourg versus unaffected facilities. Available secondary diagnostic: historical BGP-prefix visibility for OVH's entire ASN.
cases.window: period 0 = mean service availability fraction March 1–8 UTC; period 1 = March 10–17 UTC. Omit March 9 because the fire began after midnight local time March 10 (March 9 UTC). exposure fixed from pre-fire facility mapping; cluster = facility; stratum = pre-matched service category.
cases.counterfactual: Services in demonstrably unaffected facilities, with pre-matched functions, loads, and backup arrangements.
cases.prediction: Affected services lose availability and recover as physical support or backups are restored.
diagnostics: Pre-fire facility map and service availability required
Backup placement and routing spillovers
Facility-level assignment has few clusters
BGP announcements can remain intact while hosted services fail
identification_limits: AS16276 includes many unaffected facilities; it is not a Strasbourg treatment indicator
BGP prefix counts are not server uptime or AI output
No service effect is estimated from the public ASN diagnostic
A physical dependency does not establish AI/data-center inevitability or a productive growth loop
cases.data_status: RIPE historical prefix timelines available. Primary matched-facility service data still required.
